title: Gaussian Approximation Dimension Frontier for Factorial Experiments with Two Units per Cell
banked_reason: The delivered results establish a fifth-power sufficient regime, a legal deterministic third-power obstruction, and corrected observable calibration; matching approximation rates and the necessary-and-sufficient dimension criterion remain unresolved in oeq:sharp-frontier.
gap_reasons: The delivered results establish a fifth-power sufficient regime, a legal deterministic third-power obstruction, and corrected observable calibration; matching approximation rates and the necessary-and-sufficient dimension criterion remain unresolved in oeq:sharp-frontier.
paper_score_ceiling 5.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: The original marginal-only two-unit-cell assignment model yields a log5 sufficient Gaussian rectangle regime, a legal log3 necessary obstruction, and corrected observable calibration on every oracle-valid sequence. The localized signed two-row deletion/facet contraction did not close without prohibited inverse residual-variance or covariance-minor dependence, leaving the sharp frontier and full-regime raw-band question open. Math review passed with seven source attestations; independent validity consultation confirmed below-field termination at incremental, with both scope findings unrepaired.
tldr: For a binary factorial experiment with two units in every profile and possibly singular assignment covariance, this note proves a uniform Gaussian rectangle approximation under \(\log^5(2d)/N\to0\) and constructs deterministic legal tables showing that \(\log^3(2d)/N\to0\) is necessary. It also proves observable pooled-pair Gaussian multiplier bands with an explicit correction that vanishes on every oracle-valid sequence, and proves raw-band coverage in the fifth-power regime. The exact approximation frontier and raw-band validity throughout the full oracle-valid region remain open. The intended application is a prospective randomized binary-factor subset study of inflammatory priming and MSC morphology.
gap: Shi--Ding Appendix D.5, Theorem S4, treats standardized linear projections using inverse covariance. That result and independent-vector unrestricted-covariance methods do not settle the sharp all-table rectangle frontier under a marginal variance floor alone, including singular duplicate-coordinate tables.
fill: An evaluable matching approximation law, deterministic legal necessity tables, and observable centered calibration connect the dimension frontier to prospective endpoint and replication decisions.
